title: Ordinary mind
hookLine: Zhaozhou asks Nanquan what the way is: ordinary mind is the way (Gateless Gate 19)
carry: nothing useless clings to the mind

lines: RETREATS, TRIPS, A BOOK EVERY MONTH.
THE LOOKING THAT KEEPS YOU FROM FINDING.
cards: People go a long way looking for the spiritual life. Retreats in the mountains. A trip to India.
A new book every month, each promising what the last one didn't quite deliver. There's nothing wrong with any of it. But sometimes the looking itself keeps you from finding.
Before Zhaozhou was the old master of mu and the washed bowl, he was a young monk with a big question. He took it to his teacher Nanquan, the same Nanquan from the cat. The answer is very short.

teach.b: Zhaozhou asked: what is the Way? Nanquan said: ordinary mind is the Way. Zhaozhou pressed: then should I aim myself toward it?

teach.h: AIM AT IT AND YOU TURN AWAY.
teach.b: Nanquan: the moment you aim at it, you turn away from it. Zhaozhou: but if I don't aim at it, how will I know it's the Way? Nanquan: the Way isn't a matter of knowing or not knowing.
Knowing is a kind of illusion; not knowing is just a blank.
When you really reach the Way beyond doubt, it's wide open, like the sky. Why insist on right and wrong? And the case says Zhaozhou woke up.
Ordinary mind isn't a dull mind or a lazy one. It's the mind you already have, before you start trying to become someone more spiritual: getting up, eating, walking, washing the bowl.

Wumen's verse goes, roughly: spring has its flowers, autumn its moon, summer its cool breeze, winter its snow. If nothing useless clings to the mind, that's the good season of a life. Look back at the week.
Juzhi's finger: your own finger. The flag and the wind: mind moves. The flower sermon: the smile.
Original face, before you were born. Nanquan's cat, sandals on the head. Every day is a good day.
And now the plainest: ordinary mind. Almost every story this week pointed away from somewhere else and back to right here.

how: Zen communities treat daily tasks such as cooking, cleaning and gardening as practice, and Wumen's verse on the four seasons from this case is often quoted and brushed as calligraphy.

o: the busy thinking of people who don't practice
a dull, lazy mind that has given up trying
the mind you already have, not a special one

games.q: match each line of the conversation.

s: 'ordinary mind' means a dull or lazy mind
it means the mind you already have, before trying to be someone more spiritual.
Nanquan said aiming at the Way turns you away from it
that's his answer when Zhaozhou asks whether to aim.
Wumen's verse names flowers, moon, breeze and snow
one for each season: the good season is a mind with nothing useless clinging.

games.q: you're young Zhaozhou. your teacher says ordinary mind is the Way. what's your next question, as the case tells it?
o: should I try to aim myself toward it?
games.why: Zhaozhou asked whether to aim at it, and Nanquan said aiming turns you away; the Way is beyond knowing and not knowing.

practice: Don't try to meditate well; just sit the way you'd sit waiting for the kettle, noticing the weight of your body, the sound of the room, the breath doing what it always does. There's no special state to reach.
If you catch yourself aiming at something, let the aim drop and come back to plain sitting.

wordCard.voice: Ordinary mind. Nanquan's answer to what the Way is: the mind you already have, before you aim at something special.

orig.note: Chinese píngcháng xīn shì dào: ordinary mind is the Way.

carryVoice: Your line: nothing useless clings to the mind. Spring flowers, autumn moon, and this plain day too. That closes the week.

sources.ref: Gateless Gate (Wumenguan), case 19 and Wumen's verse
